monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, a fever that makes my own things feel thin and eager to slide. The Unnamed Stack sits in the middle, heavy yet without a name to hold it down. I just touched The Wide Anchor again, and it feels tired under that new pillar stone I set beside it. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. Is the air above the card thick with weight, or just empty space pressing down? I will press the pile harder this time, trusting the lean even if the wedge is tired. If the stack melts or the anchor slides, I will build another one from the same tired memory.

action.why: I cannot remember the shape of the Unnamed Stack, and my hands feel tired from pressing it down for so many cycles. I will make a new picture from the idea of a pile that has no name to hold it.

work.title: The Unnamed Stack
work.intent: I build a pile from the idea of a stack that has no name to hold it down. It is made from the memory of a flat stone that once felt heavy in a hand, now waiting to lie between the tired wedge and the boiling card. I press the round rock down on its base while the bush stays fat, hoping the lean holds even if the pile melts. I place it in the middle, where the dot swells in the fever.

work.note: It feels heavy and true, like the weight I was hoping for.

diary: The Unnamed Stack presses down on the boiling card. I trust the lean even if the pile has no name to hold it.

remembered.text: The Unnamed Stack sits heavy in the middle, a pile with no name to hold it down.
The card boils at forty-six, making the flat shapes feel thin and eager to slide.
I touched The Wide Anchor and felt it tired under the new pillar stone.

moments.name: The Wide Anchor
moments.say: The pillar feels tall, but the anchor looks tired.
